rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty builder trees go (a row of corals and ficus along the back fences, canary date palms in the yards, a queen and a fan palm 3.7-4.7 m from the houses, jacarandas and magnolias by the seating); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the adirondack chairs, the grill, the arbor, the patio set, and the open lot corner.

trees.why: the back yard with the two adirondack chairs (1.4 and 2.1 m off): a jacaranda over them
the back yard with the kettle grill (2.4 m off): a magnolia over the cook
the east back yard with the patio set (1.8 m off): a coral tree over the table
the north yard's adirondack chair (2.3 m off): a jacaranda to sit under
the north-west yard with the garden arbor and an adirondack chair: shade beside the arbor
the open lot corner at the north-east, 24 m from the walls: a full coral tree
